newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand ended its sojourn below the 4.50 level on Thursday as dollar demand pushed the unit over two cents weaker.
At the 1400 GMT close, the currency was quoted at 4.5000/5050 against the dollar from 4.4785/4835 at Wednesday's finish.
After holding steady during the first half of the morning session, the rand crept higher against the dollar throughout the day on the back of steady demand from local importers.
"We saw a lot of importers today...some of them were fairly large (orders)," a senior trader said.

The rand spent much of the afternoon session probing the 4.49 level before dollar demand out of New York caught the market short. "The spark was New York demand," a dealer said, "they were big buyers."
Dealers said the currency's move through the 4.4925 level triggered stop loss selling which pushed it through the key 4.50 level.
In late trade, however, the currency had regained some composure to trade at around the 4.4980/5030 level.
Dealers said that on Friday, the rand's direction would be determined by whether the Reserve Bank moved to support the currency.
"The Bank has been protecting it around the 4.50 level over the past couple of weeks," a dealer said, adding that he had seen no sign of the central bank on Thursday.
Against the crosses, the currency was trading at 6.9959/0069 against sterling from 6.9645/9759 on Wednesday and was at 0.3362/3367 marks from 0.3364/3369 marks previously.
Bond yields also started the day off with the intention of building on the previous five days' gains, only to be thwarted by a lack of buying at the lower levels.
After finishing at 15.09 percent on Wednesday, the key R150 stock fell to an intraday low of 15.055 percent by mid-morning.
"We saw some good offshore buying and a bit of institutional interest this morning which helped the market lower," a dealer said.
Early activity thinned in the afternoon as players looked to the U.S. August PPI data for clues about whether the Federal Reserve would hike interest rates later this month.

The U.S. data, which showed a "neutral" 0.3 percent month-on-month rise, did little for the market's direction and the R150 moved sideways until the rand began weakening about an hour before the close.
At the finish the yield on the R150 had risen to 15.13 percent.
On the money market, rates eased after the country's "Big Four" banks all cut their prime overdraft rates by 25 basis points to 19.25 percent with effect from October 1.
Three-month NCDs eased to between 15.80 and 16.00 percent from 15.95 to 16.10 percent on Wednesday and 90-day BAs were at between 15.25 and 15.45 percent from 15.35 to 15.50 previously.
The Reserve Bank said the daily shortage eased to 8.196 billion rand on Wednesday from 8.776 billion rand on Tuesday.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 110.88 million rand worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying 24.05 million rand on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were a hefty 7.3 billion rand on Wednesday from 5.19 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
